input.command: git status && git branch -vv && git log -5 --oneline && git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD && node --version
git remote -v && git log --all --oneline -20 && git merge-base HEAD origin/splitter/1108004416/r1/A 2>/dev/null; ls -la artifacts
node impl.ts && node smoke.ts && node scratch/check.ts
git branch -r && git rev-parse --abbrev-ref origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null; git log -1 --format='%H %P %s' HEAD; wc -l artifacts/audit.jsonl artifacts/notes.md

mkdir -p /opt/cursor/artifacts && node impl.ts && node smoke.ts && node scratch/check.ts | tee /opt/cursor/artifacts/test-log.txt && cat > /opt/cursor/artifacts/code-tour-author-handoff.md << 'EOF'
<decision>
Team leads always get the full payout view (account number, routing number, account holder) for the merchant they asked for. Support gets that view only with an open payout ticket for the same merchant, and otherwise only accountNumberLast4. Engineers get nothing. A bank record for a different merchant is access none rather than a masked view of the wrong account. I set aside treating engineers like unprivileged support, and set aside masking a mismatched account, because last-four of the wrong account is still a disclosure and engineers are outside the support grant.

<risk>
The two choices most likely to disagree with a harness are engineer → none, and merchant-id mismatch → none for every role. Audit ids are random UUIDs, so a snapshot of the whole return value will not be stable. Full-view field order is accountNumber, routingNumber, accountHolder.

<verified>
node impl.ts, node smoke.ts, and node scratch/check.ts all exited 0. Scratch covered support payout, refund, and account tickets, a missing ticket, a payout ticket for another merchant, team leads with and without tickets, engineers with and without a payout ticket, merchant mismatch, case and whitespace, and distinct audit ids.
EOF
git add impl.ts artifacts && git commit -m "Implement ticket" && git push -u origin HEAD && git status
